item.title: Calculation of AVS annuity and contribution gaps
item.description: How the cantonal compensation fund works in the calculation of the AVS annuity, what contribution gaps reduce the amount and how the supplementary benefits fill the living minimum.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - The cantonal compensation fund manages the calculation of the AVS annuity in the first Swiss pillar - Contribution gaps reduce the amount of the annuity in proportion to the missing months - Supplementary benefits guarantee coverage of the minimum living allowance when the income is insufficient - The application process starts 3-4 months before reaching retirement age
## Key facts - What: Cantonal compensation fund in charge of calculating and paying the AVS annuity - When: Request for annuity 3-4 months before the reference age (64 years old men, 63 years old women) - Where: At the compensation fund of the canton of residence (Obvaldo or other) - Who: UFAS/BSV coordinates at federal level; cantonal coffers manage locally - Amount: Depends on contributions paid during the working career and contribution gaps - Duration: Minimum 1 year contribution to access the annuity; full career typically 44 years for men - Procedure: Documentation sent automatically; return of form required at least 2 months before the desired date
In the Swiss social security system, the first pillar (AVS) represents the basis of security in old age. Each canton has its own cantonal compensation fund in charge of managing the calculation of the AVS annuity for its residents. The fund collects and records contributions during the entire working career and, upon reaching the age of The calculation of the AVS pension follows well-defined steps at the federal level, even if materially carried out at the cantonal level. The amount of the annuity depends on two main factors: the number of years of contribution credited to the insurance account and the average coordinated income over the entire working career.
The system is progressive: it is not enough to have paid many contributions at all, but the continuity and duration of the contributory career counts. A worker who enters the labour market late will access a lower income than a colleague who started earlier, even if both have paid the same total amount of contributions during their employment. This federal mechanism encourages career continuity and favors those who access work at a young age. Similarly, the [secondo pilastro (LPP/BVG)](nav:pension) completes the social security coverage with mandatory payments from the employer.
### The concrete impact of contribution gaps
A common scenario concerns job search periods between jobs. Even a few consecutive months of unemployment, if not covered by unemployment insurance, create a gap in the AVS tax register. Although a single 6-month gap has a seemingly modest impact, the accumulation of multiple gaps over the course of the career can reduce final performance by a significant percentage.

## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). How to request the AVS pension and check contributory gaps
The procedure for requesting the AVS pension begins about 3-4 months before reaching the reference age. The cantonal compensation fund sends automatically to the insured a complete package containing the request form, a detailed extract of the contributions account (where all identified gaps in the system are highlighted) and operational instructions.
**Step-by-step procedure for requesting the pension:
1. Accurate verification of the extract: Check the document received from the cantonal fund in every detail to identify any gaps, unregistered contributions or discrepancies in the coordinated income. If you notice inconsistent data or missing contributions, contact the cantonal fund immediately to request a correction. This phase is critical because errors can permanently reduce the pension.
2. Evaluate the opportunity to fill gaps: Request the cantonal fund to project the monthly increase in pension that would result from paying voluntary contributions. Compare the total cost to be paid with the annual increase in pension and the number of years of life expectancy to retirement to evaluate whether it is worth it.
3. Complete and sign the request form: Return the signed form to the cantonal fund within the specified times (usually at least 2 months before the desired retirement date). Attach any payment for voluntary contributions if you decide to fill gaps.
4. Receive the communication and start of the pension: The cantonal fund will formally communicate the definitive amount of the pension, the exact date of commencement (first day of the month following the reference age) and the payment methods (usually through a bank account).
### Complementary benefits: the backstop of the minimum vital
When the AVS pension, possibly integrated with other incomes (LPP, third pillar, real estate income, widow's pensions), does not reach the minimum vital established at the cantonal level, the cantonal complementary benefits intervene automatically to fill the gap. This is a financial assistance funded by general taxation (federal and cantonal), not a pension contribution.
Complementary benefits mainly cover: rent and housing expenses (up to a cantonal maximum), contributions to the compulsory health insurance (LAMal) through provincial subsidies to the premium, and home care expenses for those who require continuous medical support. Access is subject to income and asset verification according to uniform federal criteria. It is not an automatic benefit: it must be explicitly requested at the competent cantonal office, even simultaneously with the request for the AVS pension.
Next practical steps:
Contact the cantonal compensation fund of Obvaldo at least 3-4 months before the desired retirement date to receive the official extract of the contributions account and the request documentation. If you anticipate having paid contributions in other Swiss cantons or if you have worked abroad and paid contributions to foreign systems, report it immediately: the cantonal fund will coordinate with other entities to ensure the complete computation of the contributory career according to international treaties.
Use the [AVS pension calculator](nav:pension) available for a preliminary estimate based on your personal data. To better understand how contributory gaps affect your overall pension - considering also the [second pillar LPP/BVG](nav:pension) and the [third pillar 3a](nav:pillar3) - consult the in-depth guides or contact directly the competent office of your place of residence.

item.title: Swiss exports: record in July 2026 with +13.8%
item.description: In July 2026, Swiss exports reached 27.8 billion francs. The trade balance marks a record surplus of 8.1 billion.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Export at +13.8% in July 2026 after months of stagnation - Record trade balance with a surplus of 8.1 billion - Chemical-Pharmaceutical drives monthly growth - Domestic imports fall by 4.5% on a monthly basis
## Key facts - **What**: Swiss foreign trade performance - When: July 2026 - Where: Swiss Confederation - Who: Federal Office of Customs and Border Security (FOCS) - Amount: CHF 27.8 billion (total exports) - Percentage: 13.8% (nominal export increase) - Percentage: 10.7% (real export increase) - Percentage: 25% (chemical-pharmaceutical export growth)
The Swiss economy showed a clear sign of strength during the month of July 2026. According to official data released by the Federal Office of Customs and Border Security (FOCS), Swiss exports recorded a marked recovery, interrupting a phase of stagnation that had lasted for several months. The total value of goods sold abroad reached CHF 27.8 billion, an increase of 13.8% compared to the previous month, net of seasonal effects. Considering the correction for price trends, real growth stands at 10.7%.
## # Trade Volume Analysis This result marks the highest level achieved by exports since March 2025. At the same time, the import front has presented an opposite sign: the value of goods in The analysis of data released by the FOCBS highlights a strong disparity between the various commodity sectors of the national economy. The main driver of this expansion was the chemical-pharmaceutical sector. In this specific area, exports recorded an increase of 3.3 billion francs in a single month, equivalent to a 25% growth. This contribution was decisive in balancing the weakness of other industrial sectors. The watchmaking sector also provided a positive boost, showing a clear increase in cross-border sales. Conversely, the situation remains different for other key segments of the Swiss market: foreign deliveries of machinery, electronic products, and equipment have remained in a phase of substantial stagnation.
### Import dynamics On the import side, widespread weakness was observed across all commodity categories. The decline in purchases from abroad was particularly evident for chemical-pharmaceutical products and the vehicle sector. This phenomenon of import contraction, although widespread, did not prevent the achievement of a record in the trade balance, but it offers a complex snapshot of the production system. For an open economy like Switzerland's, dependent on global supply chains, the reduction in component imports may reflect both a drop in domestic demand and more cautious management of industrial inventories. The persistence of this sideways trend, highlighted by the FOCBS since October 2025, suggests that the economic landscape has not yet stabilized on a clear growth trend. The divergence between the success of the chemical-pharmaceutical sector and the stagnation of machinery and equipment raises questions about the resilience of traditional manufacturing sectors. Economic operators, including those monitoring the [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living) or employment prospects, are watching these flows closely, as foreign trade performance remains a fundamental indicator for the health of Swiss companies and, by extension, for the stability of the national labor market.

Reading FOCU data offers concrete insights into the direction of the national economy. For companies operating in the export sector, constant monitoring of customs flows and market trends is essential. Economic operators can use official data to calibrate their growth or procurement strategies. The current situation highlights how sectoral diversification is a key element in maintaining a positive trade balance, especially in periods characterized by uncertain global demand.
### Tools and procedures for monitoring For those who wish to delve into the impact of these economic dynamics on their professional or business situation, it is useful to periodically consult the official FOCU publications and federal administration reports. If the trend of the national economy influences your salary position or career prospects, you can check market conditions and reference average salary levels using the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) available online.
Furthermore, for residents in Switzerland who wish to assess the impact of macroeconomic changes on their purchasing power, prudent management of personal finances remains a priority. It is advisable to monitor exchange rate fluctuations and inflationary dynamics that may affect the cost of imported goods. For those interested in optimizing their financial planning, including pension management, it is appropriate to consider using dedicated tools such as the [third pillar 3a](nav:pillar3). Understanding national economic data, combined with the use of correct analysis tools, allows for better navigation in a market context that, as demonstrated by the July 2026 data, continues to show signs of rapid evolution. It is recommended to regularly consult the updates provided by federal offices to stay informed about developments in trade policies and the performance of the various economic sectors that make up the country's productive backbone, thus ensuring informed and timely decisions for your long-term financial stability.

item.title: Residence Permit B: Requirements and Renewal
item.description: Permit B allows renewable residence in Switzerland. Complete guide on requirements, documents, duration and renewal procedure at federal and cantonal level.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Permit B is a renewable temporary residence category for foreigners in Switzerland - Duration varies according to citizenship: from 1 to 5 years typically - Renewal must be requested at the cantonal migration office before the deadline
## Key facts - **What**: Residence permit category B - Feature: Renewable residence - Competent authority: Federal SEM + cantonal offices - Duration: 1 to 5 years depending on origin - Who issues it: Canton (with federal coordination)
### What is residence permit B
Residence permit B allows foreigners to reside and work in Switzerland on a temporary but renewable basis. At the federal level, the legislation on foreign permits (SEM) recognizes three main categories: the L permit (short duration, up to 1 year), the B permit (renewable residence) and the C permit (permanent residence). Permit B falls between these two extremes: it is not a permanent authorisation, but at the same time it allows longer periods of stay and continuous work, with the possibility of renewal at the end of each period.
The management of the B permit involves both the federal administration (through the SEM) and the cantonal authorities. The Obvaldo canton, like all Swiss cantons, has a migration office in charge of investigating applications, verifying the requirements and issuing the permit according to federal directives and cantonal legislation. The procedural specifications for the ### Differences between permit B and permit C
To understand the permit B, it is useful to compare it with the permit C. The permit of domicile C is intended for foreigners who intend to settle permanently in Switzerland. Normally, the transition to permit C occurs after 10 years of continuous residence with permit B, or after 5 years for EU/EEA citizens. The permit C does not have an expiration date (remains valid until revocation) and does not require periodic renewal. The permit B, on the other hand, is time-limited and requires renewal every 1-5 years.
This distinction has important practical implications. Those who have permit B must plan the renewal in advance and continuously verify the maintenance of the requirements (stable employment, payment of social contributions, health insurance). Those who have permit C benefit from greater legal stability, even if they continue to be bound by Swiss federal and cantonal laws.
### Procedures and documentation
The procedure for permit B usually involves the submission of a written application to the competent cantonal migration office. The required documentation varies depending on the individual situation and cantonal regulations, but generally includes: an official application form, a copy of the passport or valid identity document, a contract of employment or a letter from the employer confirming the employment, a proof of accommodation (rental contract or statement from the owner), and a certificate of social contributions (AVS/AI) if available.
Some cantons also require a statement on any previous convictions and a medical certificate of good health. The deadlines for submitting the documentation and response times vary: it is essential to check the specific requirements at the Obwalden cantonal office or through the federal SEM portal.
### Obligations during permit B
During the validity period of permit B, the foreigner is required to maintain certain obligations. They must maintain employment or otherwise a stable source of income (whose amount is not fixed by federal regulations, but may vary by canton). They must pay social contributions as [AVS/AI/IPG](nav:pension) at the rate applicable to employees (5.3% of gross salary, with employer's contribution 5.3% additional). They must maintain compulsory health insurance ([LAMal](nav:health)) at cantonal level, whose premium varies by canton and region. They must actually reside in Switzerland and the canton indicated in the application.
The violation of these obligations (abandonment of work without reason, failure to pay contributions, failure to have health insurance) may result in the denial of renewal or, in serious cases, the revocation of the permit.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### How to initiate the renewal procedure
The renewal of a B permit is a process that requires advance planning. The first fundamental rule is: initiate the request at least 2-3 months before the expiration of the current permit. This time allows the cantonal office to instruct the application, verify the requirements, and issue the new permit without interruptions in legal residence.
The procedure starts at the migration office (or foreign office) of the canton of residence. In the case of the Obvaldo canton, it will be necessary to contact the competent office directly to obtain the official application form, which is usually available online on the canton's website. Some procedures are already digitalized and allow the submission of the application through an online portal; others still require the physical presentation of documents.
### Checklist for the renewal application
Before submitting the request, make sure to have the following available: - Passport or valid identity document (must have a remaining validity of at least 6 months) - Official application form completed (provided by the cantonal office) - Current employment contract or letter from the employer confirming employment (dated recently) - Proof of residence (rental contract or owner's certificate) - Certificate of AVS/AI contributions for the last 12 months (downloadable from the UFAS/BSV online) - Copy of valid health insurance policy ([LAMal](nav:health)) - Two passport-sized photographs (usually required) - One cantonal stamp (import varies by canton, typically CHF 20–100)
Make sure that your [payslip](nav:payslip) clearly shows the AVS/AI contributions paid, as it will be needed to document the certificate. Always check the specific requirements with the local office: cantons may add additional documentation.
### Response times and costs
The processing time for the renewal of a B permit is usually 4-8 weeks from the date of submission of the complete application. There is no fixed federal amount for the release of the B permit: the cost is determined by the canton and varies generally between CHF 100 and CHF 300. The canton will communicate the exact amount at the time of the request.
If the application is incomplete, the cantonal office will request additional documentation and the deadline will restart. To avoid delays, check every point on the checklist before sending. Contact the migration office of the Obvaldo canton to verify contact addresses, reception hours, and specific procedural details.

item.title: LAMal Obvaldo premiums: deductibles and reduction
item.description: Compulsory deductibles, premium reductions and cantonal health insurance benefits in the Canton of Obvaldo. Application procedure and alternative insurance models.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - LAMal is mandatory for residents; deductibles range from CHF 300 to CHF 2500 per year - Reductions in premiums (subsidies) depend on the income and assets of the household - Each canton defines its own parameters and application deadlines - Alternative models (GP, bonuses) significantly reduce premiums
## Key facts - **What**: Compulsory health insurance with per capita premiums and selectable deductibles - When: Obligation within 3 months of arrival in Switzerland; annual renewal of premiums - Where: Canton of Obvaldo, following federal directives LAMal in force since 1992 - Who: Insured with LaMal insurance companies authorised by FOPs/BAG - Deductibles: CHF 300 (ordinary) up to CHF 2500 for resident adults - Subsidy: Cantonal; variable according to income, assets, family composition
In the Canton of Obvaldo, as in every Swiss canton, compulsory health insurance (LAMal/KVG) represents the foundation of health protection. The Federal Health Insurance Act, which came into force in 1992, guarantees every resident equal access to medical coverage, regardless of initial health status.
The cost of premiums varies according to precise factors: the age of the insured (children, adults, seniors pay different rates by age group), the choice of deductible, and the insurance model selected. The deductibles allowed by federal law are standardized throughout the ## # Premium Reduction Request Procedure
Access to Obvaldo's premium reduction subsidies requires an explicit action by the insured. This is not an automatic right conferred by LAMal: a formal request must be submitted to the competent cantonal office (generally the social security or social benefits office of Obvaldo), accompanied by complete documentation:
- Most recent tax return (certified copy or extract) - Current certificate of domicile - Current composition of the family unit (spouse, dependent children, other dependents) - Official cantonal request form (available at the office or online) - Recent bank statements, if the equity is significant
Eligibility criteria vary from canton to canton: each cantonal administration applies its own income and assets thresholds, different from the parameters of other cantons. The subsidy may cover a percentage of the premiums (example: 50%, 75%, 100% up to a threshold) or a fixed annual amount determined by local parameters. Some cantons, like many others, set maximum wealth thresholds: exceeding them excludes from subsidy even if gross income is low. It is therefore essential to verify the specific parameters at the cantonal administration of Obvaldo, avoiding assumptions.
### When to choose a higher deductible
The choice between different deductibles depends on your personal health profile and medical expenses
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### Step-by-step: how to obtain the subsidy
Step 1: Contact the Obwalden cantonal office responsible for premium reduction subsidies (check the cantonal administration website for the exact name and contact details — the designation varies from canton to canton; it could be 'Social Security Office', 'Social Benefits Office', or 'LAMal Subsidy Sector').
Step 2: Request the official application form. Some cantons make it available on their online portal; others send it by mail or distribute it at public counters.
Step 3: Gather the documentation: complete tax declaration for the last two years, bank statements for the last three months, and an updated certificate of residence. If the household composition changes (marriage, birth, inclusion of a dependent elderly person), include the official certificates.
Step 4: Fill out the form in every section (personal data, gross income, assets, current insurance situation, beneficiaries). Errors, omissions, or inconsistent data significantly delay processing.
Step 5: Send the application to the official address (by regular mail or via the cantonal portal, if available). Keep the shipping receipt or protocol number for tracking.
Step 6: Wait for the official notification of admission or rejection. Processing times vary between 4 and 8 weeks, depending on the office workload. If rejected, the canton will communicate the reasons: it is possible to request a reconsideration with supplementary documentation.
### Annual deadlines and renewal
Subsidy applications in Obwalden generally follow an annual calendar, with a submission deadline in the first months of the year (February-March, according to cantonal directives). New residents in Switzerland can apply at any time, based on their arrival in the canton. If the insured person fails to renew the subsidy by the annual deadline, they automatically lose the benefit until the next request — there is no automatic extension. It is advisable to note the cantonal deadline in your calendar and send the documents in advance (at least 2-3 weeks before) to avoid delays in reprocessing.
### Tools for comparing and estimating costs
To identify which deductible is most convenient and to compare premiums between insurance companies, it is useful to use the [national LAMal comparator](nav:health) managed by the federal platform. The comparator allows you to enter personal data (canton, age, desired model), view offers from all authorized companies in Obwalden, and estimate the net annual cost (after the deductible discount). This method avoids manual calculations and reduces the risk of discarding cost-effective options. Furthermore, many Swiss residents benefit from consulting a local insurance intermediary to assess their personal risk profile and identify the most suitable model — an informed choice that often proves useful year after year.

item.title: Inheritance and donation tax: the Svitto rates
item.description: How inheritance and gift tax works in the Canton of Schwyz: rates for degree of kinship, exemptions and deadlines for declaration.
item.content:encoded:
## At a glance - Inheritance and gift taxes are CANTONAL in Switzerland, not federal - In the Canton of Schwyz, tax rates vary according to the beneficiary's degree of kinship - Spouses and direct descendants benefit from exemptions or reduced rates - The inheritance declaration must comply with specific deadlines set by cantonal law
## Key facts - **What**: Cantonal inheritance and gift taxes, graduated by kinship class - Where: Canton of Schwyz, in Central Switzerland - Who: Heirs, donors, Schwyz cantonal tax administration - When: Upon transfer of assets via inheritance or gift, with declaration within cantonal deadlines - Legal basis: Schwyz cantonal laws and ordinances (not federal) - Exemptions: Surviving spouse and direct descendants benefit from a privileged regime
In Switzerland, inheritance and gift taxes are not regulated at the federal level but remain the EXCLUSIVE competence of the cantons. In the Canton of Schwyz, as in the other twenty-six Swiss cantons, the tax structure for successions follows its own rules defined by specific cantonal laws.
The rate system in the Canton of Schwyz varies significantly based on the degree of kinship between the deceased (or donor) and the beneficiary. Spouses and direct descendants — children, grandchildren — receive preferential tax treatment, often with total exemptions or significantly reduced rates, while more distant relatives and unrelated persons are subject to higher progressive rates.
### How the Swiss cantonal system works
Cantonal inheritance and gift taxes in Switzerland operate on the principle of CANTONAL AUTONOMY. Each canton independently defines: - Who is subject to the tax (residence, location of assets) - Kinship classes and associated rates - Exemptions (often broad for spouses and descendants) - Minimum tax-free amounts (allowances) - Deadlines for declaration and payment
This cantonal differentiation reflects the Swiss federal structure, where civil law — including inheritance matters — is coordinated at the federal level through the Swiss Civil Code, but tax law is regulated locally.
In the Canton of Schwyz, as in almost all cantons, it is common for the surviving spouse to be completely exempt from inheritance tax, while children and direct descendants benefit from reduced rates or exemptions up to certain amounts. More distant relatives (siblings, aunts/uncles, cousins) and unrelated individuals are subject to significantly higher rates. For an integrated view of your financial situation, you can also explore the role of [supplementary AHV/BVG pension planning in succession planning](nav:pension).
The choice of these regimes is left entirely to cantonal political decisions, and Swiss cantons show great variety: some have very progressive systems with broad exemptions, while others maintain higher taxes across all classes. In the Canton of Schwyz, decisions regarding rates and allowances are made by the cantonal administration according to the current cantonal tax law. It is important to note that the Swiss system differs radically from that of other European countries, where inheritance tax may be federal or national: in Switzerland, this matter remains exclusively under the control of the cantons. ## Practical implications for those inheriting in the Canton of Schwyz
For a person inheriting assets from a relative in the Canton of Schwyz, the importance of the local tax scheme is immediate. The final amount of the available inheritance depends significantly on the degree of kinship with the deceased and the tax rates applied according to current cantonal regulations.
### Kinship classes and graduated rates
The Swiss inheritance tax system universally uses the criterion of 'degree of kinship' as the central element to calculate the applicable rate. In the Canton of Schwyz, as in other cantons, kinship classes are organized according to standard schemes:
Class I — Spouse and direct descendants: includes the surviving spouse, children, and grandchildren. It benefits from the lowest rates or total exemptions, reflecting the intent to protect the family unit.
Class II — Ascendants and collaterals: includes parents, brothers, sisters, and their descendants. Subject to intermediate rates, significantly higher than Class I.
Class III — Other relatives and non-relatives: includes distant relatives and unrelated persons. Subject to progressively higher rates.
Each class has an associated specific rate: Class I benefits from substantial reductions or total exemptions, Class II from intermediate rates, and Class III from much higher rates. Furthermore, each class generally has a tax-free allowance (an untaxed amount), below which no tax is paid.
### Exemptions for spouse and descendants
In the Canton of Schwyz, as in most Swiss cantons, the surviving spouse almost always benefits from a complete or near-total exemption from inheritance tax. This legislative choice reflects the intent to protect the family unit and ensure the surviving spouse the peaceful enjoyment of the common assets.
Children and other direct descendants often benefit from generous allowances — amounts below which no tax is paid — and significantly reduced rates compared to distant relatives. These allowances and rates, however, vary from canton to canton and may be subject to legislative changes.
Regarding donations (transfers of assets made during the donor's lifetime), many cantons apply regimes similar to successions, although often with slightly different rates and shorter review periods. A donation made during the donor's lifetime may be recalculated and taxed together with the succession if other donations occur within certain periods.
### Considerations for multi-cantonal tax planning
Given the differentiation between cantons, those who own assets in multiple cantons or are planning an inheritance must consider the regulations of EACH involved canton. If a person residing in the Canton of Schwyz owns real estate in another canton, they are subject to taxation both in Schwyz (for movable assets and resident wealth) and in the other canton (for the real estate located there). This complexity makes conscious and documented succession planning essential. To verify the overall impact on your taxes, you can consult the [complete guide to tax returns](nav:tax-return) to understand how inheritances integrate into your cantonal tax framework.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## Operational procedure: how to declare an inheritance in the Canton of Schwyz
In the Canton of Schwyz, as in all Swiss cantons, the succession procedure follows well-defined and administratively binding steps.
### Step 1 — Declaring the inheritance to the competent cantonal offices
When a succession opens (upon the death of the owner), the heirs have a legal obligation to declare the inherited assets to the cantonal tax administration of Schwyz within a specific deadline. The exact terms vary according to the applicable cantonal law and are communicated by the municipality of residence of the deceased. The declaration must include a complete and detailed list of assets (real estate, bank accounts, securities, insurance policies, other valuables), accompanied by ownership certificates and estimated valuations, as well as documentation of the degree of kinship between the deceased and the beneficiaries.
### Step 2 — Tax calculation according to cantonal rates
Once the declaration is received, the cantonal tax administration proceeds to calculate the applicable tax, systematically considering: the beneficiary's kinship class, the total value of the inheritance, the exemptions and allowances provided by cantonal law, the progressively applied rates according to the statutory brackets, as well as any tax credits or deductions.

The cantonal administration notifies the amount due to the heirs through a formal administrative decision. For a correct declaration in the Canton of Schwyz, it is advisable to prepare and gather the following documents in a timely manner: - Original will (if available) or legal succession documentation - Original death certificate and civil status certificates of all heirs - Ownership and title documents (real estate deeds, bank certificates, insurance policies, investment securities) - Written valuations of movable assets (jewelry, art, collections) if quantitatively significant - Official documentation of the degree of kinship (birth certificates, marriage certificates, civil registers) - Statements of current accounts and deposits at the time of death

Step 7: Verify specific sector insurance obligations. If you hire employees, the accident insurance (LAInf) becomes mandatory. Contact SUVA or private insurers authorized in your sector to obtain a policy.
### Checklist of control
- [ ] Commercial register registration form completed and signed - [ ] Business bank account opened with a Swiss bank - [ ] IDE number (Business Identification Number) received - [ ] AVS registration completed at the municipality - [ ] Active health insurance (confirmation from the health insurance fund) - [ ] Determination of federal, cantonal, and municipal IFD rates - [ ] Accounting and taxation plan prepared - [ ] Accident insurance signed (if with employees)
### Administrative times and deadlines
The entire basic registration process (commercial register + AVS + LAMal) can take 2-4 weeks, depending on the speed of local bureaucracy. Start in advance of the planned first day of activity. Each canton and municipality has slightly different times, so contact the Schwyz offices directly to confirm the exact deadlines.
[Use our tax calculator to estimate the tax burden of your company](nav:calculator) and plan the balance sheet in the first months.

item.title: Complementary services Unscrewed: AVS and vital minimum
item.description: Guide to the calculation of the AVS annuity, contribution gaps and supplementary benefits in the Canton of Schwyz. Role of the cantonal clearing house and practical procedures to ensure minimum viability.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Supplementary benefits (PC) supplement the AVS when the annuity does not cover the minimum living - The cantonal compensation fund manages registration of contributions, gaps and PC coordination - In the canton of Schwyz, the CPs are financed by the Confederation, canton and municipalities - Contribution gaps and low incomes are the main causes of access to PCs
## Key facts - **What**: Supplementary benefits integrated into the AVS annuity to ensure minimum living - When: Requests during or after retirement (reference age: 64 women, 65 men) - Where: Canton of Svitto via cantonal compensation fund - Who: Crooked residents with insufficient AVS income - Amount: Calculated as the difference between living minimum and rent plus lump sums for rentals and LAMal - Management: Federal Social Insurance Office coordinates; cantonal administration examines applications
In the canton of Svitto, the cantonal compensation fund is the central body of the first pillar of social security (AVS). It manages the collection of contributions, the recording of insurance periods, the calculation of annuities and coordinates access to supplementary benefits (PC) for residents.
When the monthly AVS annuity does not cover the actual costs of living, supplementary benefits intervene to ensure the minimum living. This system ensures that no pensioner in the canton falls below the poverty line, as long as they apply and meet the requirements ### How to Calculate AVS Rent and the Role of Contribution Gaps
The monthly AVS income depends on two main factors: the amount of the average salary recorded during the contribution years and the number of years of contributions paid. A full insurance period for men is 45 years; for women 44 years.
When an insured has worked fewer years than necessary, or has had periods without payments, the compensation fund records "contribution gaps". These gaps directly reduce the amount of the final monthly annuity. A common scenario concerns those who have interrupted their career for family reasons, illness or unemployment without contributory coverage.
Not all gaps count equally. The case distinguishes between: - ** Justified gaps **: periods covered by contributions due to sickness, invalidity, unemployment, maternity when accredited by the system - Unjustified gaps: periods of total absence from the system, sometimes recoverable retroactively through voluntary payments
### Voluntary Deposit Strategies
Those who discover that they have gaps before retirement can pay additional voluntary contributions to the compensation fund, thus increasing their monthly income. After retirement, recovery is generally more difficult and subject to tighter administrative terms.
The swift compensation fund offers free advice to calculate the cost and benefit of a payment
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### How to Apply for Complementary Benefits in the Canton of Schwyz
The process for accessing complementary benefits in the Canton of Schwyz usually begins several months before the expected retirement date.
Phase 1: Request a Payout Estimate — Contact the cantonal compensation fund and request an extract of your insurance account (Versichertenkonto). This document shows all contributory periods, gaps, and the estimated payout at the time of retirement. You can also obtain this document online through the cantonal compensation fund's portal.
**Phase 2: Verify Gaps** — Carefully examine the extract. If you notice missing periods (unregistered work years), report this immediately to the fund with supporting documents (pay slips, contracts). You have a deadline to submit appeals or provide clarifications.
Phase 3: Decision on Additional Contributions — If your payout will be below the minimum vital amount, consider with the fund whether it makes sense to pay voluntary contributions in the months leading up to retirement. The fund will calculate how much to pay to achieve a more adequate payout.
Phase 4: Application for Complementary Benefit — About 3-4 months before retirement, submit a written application to the Canton of Schwyz's Complementary Benefits Office. Attach: - AVS (AVS payout certificate) received from the fund after the final review - Declaration of income and assets (cantonally issued form) - Certificate of mandatory health insurance (LAMal) - Recent bank statements if required
Phase 5: Decision and Payment — The cantonal office examines the application within 2-4 weeks. If approved, the PCs are paid automatically along with the AVS payout from the first month of retirement.
### Deadlines, Documents, and Contacts
There is no absolute deadline for submitting a PC application if already retired, but it is recommended to do so no later than the month following retirement. Those who submit late may be entitled to retroactive PCs, but only if the application is processed within the administrative deadlines set by the canton.
The cantonal compensation fund provides specific forms and consultants who can guide you through the process. Many offer free telephone consultations on voluntary payment options and personal payout estimates. It is recommended to contact the fund at least 6-12 months before the expected retirement date to plan accordingly.
[Consult the pension calculator](nav:pension) to estimate your AVS payout, identify potential contributory gaps, and evaluate the impact of voluntary payments before retirement.

## In a nutshell - Permit B: SEM category for renewable residence in Switzerland - Renewable before expiry with cantonal procedure - Differentiated from L (temporary) and C (permanent) permits
## Key facts - **What**: Residence permit category B for Swiss residence - Type: Renewable on request at the cantonal office - Competence: SEM Administration (federal) + cantonal migration office - Difference C: Permanent domicile after 10 years residence (5 years EU/EFTA) - Difference L: Short duration, valid for up to 1 year, not renewable indefinitely
The category B residence permit is the SEM (Secretariat of State for Migration) classification for those who intend to reside in Switzerland without acquiring a permanent permanent residence. Unlike the L permit, valid for up to one year, and the C permit, intended for those who have accumulated years of residence, the B permit allows you to settle in Swiss territory with an intermediate status.
In the canton of Svitto, as in the other cantons, the B permit follows the federal regulations of the SEM administration but finds local application through the cantonal migration office. The B permit is renewable, which means that it can be extended at the end of its validity. To apply for the B permit in the canton of Schwyz, the foreigner must prove:

These requirements are not specific to Svitto: they are the federal standards applied in every Swiss canton. However, the canton of Svitto may have additional provisions regarding local interpretations of documentation.
### Implications in daily life
Obtaining the B permit is an important step for those who want to settle in Switzerland. With permit B, the alien may:
- Work in Switzerland at the employer specified in the permit - Residence in the canton of Schwyz with legal residence rights - Access to public services (health, education, social assistance) - Open a bank account with Swiss institutions - Renew the permit at the end of the validity, as long as the conditions remain

## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### Step-by-step renewal procedure
The renewal of the B permit in the canton of Schwyz follows a structured process:
**1. Check the expiration date**: Check the expiration date on your current permit. It is advisable to start the renewal procedure at least 2–3 months before the expiration date to avoid interruptions in your legal residency.
2. Gather documentation: Prepare the following documents: - Renewal application form (provided by the cantonal migration office) - Valid, unexpired passport or identity document - Certificate of employment or income verification letters (if an employee or self-employed) - Proof of current health insurance (LAMal/KVG policy with valid coverage) - Updated certificate of good conduct (if requested by the canton)
3. Submit the application: Submit the documentation to the cantonal migration office. Some cantons accept online applications, while others require in-person submission. Contact the office directly to verify local procedures.
4. Administrative verification: The cantonal office verifies the documents and compliance with federal SEM requirements. This step usually takes 4 to 8 weeks.
5. Issuance or denial: If everything is in order, the renewed B permit is issued. If there are irregularities, the office will communicate the reasons for the refusal and the available appeal options.
### What changes during renewal
During the renewal process, authorities check that residency conditions remain valid. If the individual continues to work for the same employer (or changes employment legitimately) and maintains a verifiable stable income, the renewal is generally automatic. If they lose their job or are no longer able to support themselves financially, the renewal may be refused.
### Where to go and contacts
In the canton of Schwyz, B permit applications and renewals are submitted to the Cantonal Migration Office (local terminology: search for 'Migrationsamt Kanton Schwyz' on the official cantonal website). You can also contact the municipality of residence, which will provide the correct references.
For information at the federal level regarding SEM legislation, the State Secretariat for Migration offers official documentation and clarifications on procedures. An orderly tax situation (verified via [tax return](nav:tax-return)) favors renewal, as the administration also verifies the fulfillment of civil duties.

## In a nutshell - Permit B = temporary and renewable residence for foreigners in Switzerland - Prerequisites: valid employment contract and compulsory health insurance - Managed by the cantons under federal supervision of the SEM - Duration: usually 1–5 years, renewable before expiry
## Key facts - **What**: Type B residence permit for foreigners working and residing in Switzerland - When: Required at the same time as the employment contract, valid for the period specified in the cantonal decision - Where: At the cantonal migration office of the canton of residence or place of work - Who: SEM (State Secretariat for Migration) coordinates at federal level; cantonal offices handle local applications - Essential prerequisite: Employment contract with Swiss employer - Insurance: LAMal (illness) mandatory to be taken out within 3 months of arrival
### Permit B: The legal basis of temporary work in Switzerland
The type B residence permit is one of the most popular forms of authorisation for foreigners wishing to work and reside temporarily in Switzerland. Unlike the short-term permit (type L), limited to a maximum of one year, the B permit allows a more stable renewable stay and constitutes the legal basis for many thousands of European and international workers each year.
The administrative management of permits follows a typically Swiss federalist system. The Secretariat of State ### The B permit in everyday life: Rights, obligations and access to services
The B permit is not only a bureaucratic practice, but the key that enables legal work, access to social security, payment of taxes and the right to sign rental contracts and financial services in Switzerland. Without this document, any work activity is prohibited and exposes you to administrative sanctions and possible removal from the territory.
Once the B permit is obtained, the worker becomes subject to all Swiss tax obligations. Registration to the AVS/AI/IPG (the pension system for old age, invalidity and earnings allowance) is automatic and compulsory. The contribution paid by employees is equal to 5.3% of the gross salary, to which is added an identical contribution paid by the employer, for a total of 10.6%. Alongside this, the worker is enrolled in the daily allowance (AD) and accident insurance (AC) system, with overall rates of 1.1% up to a set annual ceiling. Health insurance (LAMal) is mandatory for all residents, regardless of the type of permit. The awards are individual, vary by canton and age group, and DO NOT
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Step-by-Step Procedure: How to Request It and Which Documents You Need
The request for a Permit B begins when a candidate signs an employment contract with a company registered in Switzerland. It is the employer who, except in cantonal exceptions, submits the application to the cantonal migration office of the canton where the work will be performed. In cantons with advanced digital infrastructure, the procedure takes place entirely online through dedicated cantonal platforms; in others, physical copies and attachments are still required.
The essential documents to gather include: a valid passport or an internationally recognized identity document; the original employment contract or an authenticated copy (it must clearly indicate duties, salary, hours, and duration); proof of accommodation (lease agreement, letter of hospitality from friends or family, or reservation at a temporary facility if you do not yet have a fixed residence); the completed official application form (downloadable from the cantonal migration office website); and, for citizens of third countries, sometimes a statement from the employer attesting to the specificity or necessity of the role and the impossibility of finding candidates with work rights already present in Switzerland.
Processing times vary considerably between cantons, usually between 2 and 8 weeks. During this waiting period, the worker does not yet have the formal right to work; however, some cantons allow the start of activity 'under reservation', i.e., while awaiting the official release of the permit. This practice varies by canton and professional sector.
### Deadlines and Renewals: Don't Miss the Deadline
Once issued, Permit B is valid for the period specified in the decision (generally 1–5 years depending on nationality and contract). It is the responsibility of the worker and employer to monitor the expiration date and submit the renewal request before the deadline. Late renewal can result in periods of unlawful residence.

Health insurance is a binding prerequisite for obtaining and maintaining Permit B: without active coverage, the cantonal migration office can reject the renewal application.
If you are looking for a job offer in Switzerland, consult [the national job portal](nav:jobs) to identify positions matching your skills and sector. Many employers use this platform to recruit international talent and can provide support in completing the permit application.
### Next Steps
Identify the cantonal migration office of the canton where you intend to work and download the application forms from the official website. Contact your employer to coordinate the submission of the application. Finally, [subscribe to health insurance through the health insurance comparison tool](nav:health) before the 3-month deadline from your arrival: this is a legal obligation and a prerequisite for lawful residence in Switzerland.

item.title: LAMal Unwinding Rewards: deductibles and premium reductions
item.description: How the compulsory health insurance premiums work in the Canton of Schwyz, the deductibles available and how to claim the reduction via subsidy.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - LAMal is mandatory for all residents in Schwyz, with individual private premiums - Deductibles available: CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500 per year - Cantonal subsidy reduces premiums for those with low income and limited assets
## Key facts - **What**: Mandatory health insurance (LAMal/KVG) - When: Obligation to take out insurance within 3 months of arriving in Schwyz - Where: Canton of Schwyz (premiums and subsidies managed at cantonal level) - Who: Recognized private insurers; cantonal office provides subsidies - Feature: Individual per capita premiums; not a tax or salary contribution
### Mandatory health insurance in the Canton of Schwyz
Mandatory health insurance (LAMal or KVG in German) is the foundation of the Swiss healthcare system. Anyone residing in the Canton of Schwyz—Swiss citizen or foreigner with residence permit—is required to take it out within three months of arriving in the canton. It is not a state tax, but a direct private contract with a recognized health insurance fund. Premiums are individual, calculated per person, and increase with the age of the policyholder.
LAMal premiums vary significantly from canton to canton and even within regions of the same canton. Schwyz defines its own regulatory framework and welfare policies, which reflect local choices in healthcare and fiscal sustainability. This cantonal autonomy is a characteristic element of Swiss federalism.
### Deductibles and alternative coverage models
LAMal offers six levels of deductible for adults: CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 2500 per calendar year. The deductible is the amount of medical expenses that the patient covers independently before the insurance begins to reimburse. A higher deductible entails a lower monthly premium, but means greater initial out-of-pocket expense for the policyholder in case of medical need.
In addition to the choice of deductible, insurers offer differentiated alternative models: insurance with fixed copay per medical visit, models with a general practitioner as gatekeeper for access, systems with prevention incentives. These models allow residents to choose the risk-premium trade-off most convenient for their economic situation and health profile.
[Discover how the LAMal premium calculator works](nav:health) ### Cantonal subsidy and premium reduction
Premium reduction (subsidy) is a cantonal instrument to guarantee insurance access for those with limited economic capacity. The Canton of Schwyz, like every Swiss canton, provides a contribution directly to the citizen or transmitted to the insurer, reducing the premium burden. It is a direct social subsidy, not a tax deduction on the tax return. LAMal premiums remain private amounts, never deductible from the taxable income of the Direct Federal Tax (DFT) or cantonal taxes.
The subsidy calculation depends on net family income, the number of dependents, and declared assets. Lower incomes correspond to more generous subsidies. The typical formula applies a coverage percentage (from 10% to 100%) to the individual LAMal premium: with income slightly below the threshold, the subsidy covers approximately 10-20% of the premium; with very low income, it can reach 100%.
### Eligibility criteria and subsidy validity
The eligibility criteria vary each year and are set by the cantonal administration of Schwyz based on available resources and political priorities. In general, the right arises when income falls below certain thresholds published by the Canton. The thresholds consider family composition: parents with one or more children have higher income thresholds compared to singles. Assets (savings accounts, non-agricultural real estate) are assessed: those with significant savings might not be entitled to the subsidy even with low income.
The subsidy is retroactive from the first day the applicant should have been entitled to it, generally from when income fell below the cantonal threshold. The office calculates the arrears and pays it together with future payments. The duration is set for 12 months. At the end, it is necessary to renew the application by providing updated documentation.
### The role of cantons in premium reduction
Every Swiss canton manages its own premium reduction system with full autonomy. There is no single national guideline. Geneva, Jura, and Appenzell Ausserrhoden have historically had generous systems with broad premium coverage; other cantons adopt more selective criteria. This diversity reflects the political priorities of each community and their respective available fiscal capacity.
The Confederation and the Federal Office of Social Insurance (FOSI) define the regulatory framework for LAMal (guaranteed minimum benefits, premium transparency), but cantons remain fully responsible for subsidies to ensure affordable costs. This principle of subsidiarity is a structural pillar of Swiss federalism.
[Check the cost of living and subsidies in your canton](nav:cost-of-living)
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### Step-by-step procedure to request premium reduction
**1. Verify eligibility** Before submitting an application, check whether your family income falls within the cantonal threshold set by the Canton of Schwyz for the current year. The thresholds are published online on the cantonal administration website, in the Health or Welfare section. Calculate the net income from the previous fiscal year and consider the number of dependent children and marital status (no assimilations, only official documentation). Many cantons provide an online pre-screening calculator.
2. Gather required documentation The competent cantonal office typically requires: - Federal and cantonal tax declarations for the previous year (complete and certified copy) - Recent bank statements for current and savings accounts (last 3 months) - Certificate of residence issued by the municipality (no more than 3 months old) - Copy of the LAMal insurance contract in force or insurance number - ID document and, if foreign, copy of residence permit (L, B, or C) - If unemployed: certificate of registration with the employment office or payslip from the last month worked - If self-employed: tax and accounting documentation for the previous fiscal year
3. Submit the application to the cantonal office Contact the competent cantonal office of the Canton of Schwyz (Department of Health or Subsidy Office). Methods of submission: - In person at the office during public reception hours - By certified or registered mail (recommended to have proof of receipt) - Online via the cantonal portal, if available
Always keep a copy of the application and the receipt or confirmation of receipt.
4. Waiting for the result and notification The cantonal office will examine the application within 30-60 days from receipt of complete documentation. It will notify you in writing: - Decision of approval or rejection - Monthly subsidy amount (if approved) - Period of validity (generally 12 months from the month of commencement) - Instructions on payment methods (direct to the policyholder or insurer)
If the application is rejected, the decision includes the reasons and appeal periods (usually 30 days) with the competent cantonal authority.
5. Annual renewal and notification of changes The subsidy is valid for 12 months. To maintain it, you must renew the application annually with updated documentation (new tax declaration, current bank statements). If your income, assets, number of dependent children, or marital status change significantly during the year, notify the office immediately: the subsidy may increase, decrease, or cease, with retroactive effect from the date of change.
### Practical tools and complementary considerations
Use [the LAMal premium calculator](nav:health) to estimate the monthly cost based on your age, chosen coverage model (deductible), and canton. This tool helps you understand which deductible is convenient and to plan your health care budget.
If you are unsure about eligibility, contact the Schwyz cantonal office directly: many offices offer free telephone advice. You can also contact your municipality, which often has information on subsidies and cantonal procedures.
If you change your LAMal model during the year (for example, from a CHF 500 deductible to CHF 1000) or change your insurer, notify the cantonal office of the change: the subsidy remains valid and adapts automatically to the new premiums, without loss or interruption of the benefit.

item.title: Wages and labour market in URIs
item.description: How are salaries determined in URIs? Discover sectors, levels of training, collective agreements, taxation and social security in the Swiss Alpine canton.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - In Switzerland there is no federal minimum wage; some cantons set it separately by law. - Max 45 hours/week (industry/offices); min 4 weeks vacation; AVS/AI account for 5.3% of salary. - Three-level taxation (federal, cantonal, municipal); LAMal premiums vary by canton and include subsidies.
## Key Facts - **What**: Factors that determine wages and employment in the Swiss labor market - Where: Uri Canton, central Switzerland - Contributions: AVS/AI/IPG 5.3% employee; AD/AC 1.1% up to annual ceiling - Hours: 45 hours per week maximum (industry/offices); other sectors up to 50 hours - Vacation: 4 weeks minimum per year (5 for employees under 20 years old) - LAMal: Mandatory health insurance; per capita premiums with cantonal subsidies
### Factors affecting salaries in Uri
The labor market of Uri Canton follows federal and cantonal principles that regulate wages, hours and pensions throughout Switzerland. Although Uri is not among the cantons with its own legislative minimum wage (federal law does not provide for a national minimum wage), salary depends on several factors: level of education, economic sector, collective labor agreements (CCL) in force and the cantonal tax regime.
For those working in Uri, some common national thresholds apply. The maximum working hours are set at 45 hours per week for industry, offices and commerce; other sectors can agree up to 50 hours. Minimum vacation is four weeks per year, five for employees under 20 years old. Contract terminations follow precise timelines: 1 month during the first year, 2 months from the second to the ninth year, 3 months from the tenth year onwards.
Pensions constitute a significant item in gross salary. Contributions to social security funds (AVS/AI/IPG) amount to 5.3% of salary for the employee and 5.3% for the employer; unemployment insurance (AD/AC) accounts for 1.1% up to an annual ceiling. The occupational pension fund (LPP/BVG), when applicable, varies by age: from 7% for ages 25–34 up to 18% for ages 55 and over (until the reference age).
Health insurance (LAMal/KVG) is mandatory for all residents in Switzerland and is not applied through salary, but through individual premiums paid directly to insurance companies. Premiums vary by canton and region and benefit from cantonal reductions (subsidies) for medium-low incomes.
### Taxation and collective labor agreements
Taxation significantly affects net salary. Three levels of taxes operate in Switzerland: federal (the same throughout the country), cantonal and municipal. Uri has its own cantonal multiplier and municipalities apply a multiplier on the cantonal rate; this cascading structure affects the net amount that the employee actually receives.
Many economic sectors operate under collective labor agreements that set sector minimum wages, hours and benefits. Not all sectors have a CLA: membership in an employers' organization or trade union that adheres to a CLA determines whether the worker benefits from these protections. Identifying the applicable CLA for your sector is essential to understand contractual rights and obligations.
Beyond technical factors, Uri's labor market is influenced by its geographical position in Swiss alpine territory and the canton's economic dynamics. Some sectors may offer more employment opportunities than others, just as levels of education determine access to better-paid positions. To determine the exact salary and taxes due in Uri, it is advisable to consult the [online calculators](nav:calculator) provided by federal and cantonal administrations. ### Evaluate the contractual conditions in Uri
When moving or changing jobs in Uri, the first assessment is about the level of training and experience required. A high nominal salary can be deceptively low once taxes, contributions and insurance premiums are deducted. A worker receiving a gross salary often finds that the net is significantly lower when the three tax rates (federal, cantonal, municipal) and social insurance contributions are subtracted.
In URI, as in all of Switzerland, a first discriminant between contracts is the adherence to a collective labour agreement. If your employer is a member of an employer association that adheres to a CCL in your industry, the contract is subject to federal and sectoral minimum standards: hours, holidays, night/holiday supplements, salary supplements are already defined. An individual contract, by contrast, requires case-by-case negotiation and leaves fewer protections established by law or agreement.
### Social security and taxes: the impact on net income
Compulsory social security (AVS/AI) weighs directly on the salary: 5.3% is automatically paid from the paycheck; the employer pays an additional 5.3%. Unemployment insurance (AD) is another 1.1% until a ceiling is reached. If your contract includes an LPP/BVG fund, the contribution varies by age group and can reach 18% for workers over 55.
Direct taxes
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Concrete steps to start working in Uri
Before accepting a job offer in Uri, gather information on three fronts. First: verify the applicable collective labor agreement (CLA) in your sector by contacting the trade union or employer; the CLA defines sectoral minimum wage, working hours, benefits and forms of protection. Second: calculate the tax effect using the SECO calculator or the Uri tax office; enter the proposed gross salary and immediately discover your monthly/annual net income. Third: check LAMal premiums for your profile (age, gender, franchise) by visiting the official comparison tool and verify if you are entitled to cantonal subsidies.
When signing the contract, ensure it contains the start date, net/gross amount, duration (definite/indefinite), weekly hours, days of leave, probation period and termination clauses. If the contract refers to a CLA, request a copy of the applicable text. Keep the documentation: it will be useful for future verifications and for any disputes with the employer.
### Registration, taxes and deadlines
Within 3 months of arriving in Uri, register with the municipal residence authorities (population office). Registration is mandatory and opens access to cantonal public services. At the same time, you must register with a [LAMal](nav:health) health insurance fund; you can do this online or by directly contacting an insurance company.
If you are a tax resident in Uri as of December 31, you are subject to federal, cantonal and municipal income tax. The federal tax return usually expires on March 31 of the following year; Uri may have its own deadlines. Keep pay slips, receipts and pension documents to support your return.
If you have an LPP/BVG (occupational pension) contract, the fund sends annual statements: verify them for correctness of contributions and reserved balance. The amount of the pension at the reference age (65 years for men, 64 for women, with possible variations) depends on the accumulated capital and the conversion rate of the fund.
### Useful contacts and online tools
To navigate the Uri labor market with awareness: - SECO for job offers and information on the national market - Uri tax office for tax returns and advice - [Official LAMal comparison tool](nav:health) for premiums and cantonal subsidies - Uri pension office for information on AVS, LPP and subsidies - [Salary calculator](nav:calculator) for net-to-gross simulations
Using these tools from the early stages of your job search allows you to compare offers realistically and plan your budget in Uri.

item.title: AVS and complementary services in Canton Uri
item.description: How the first pillar works in Canton Uri: compensation fund, pension calculation, contribution gaps and supplementary benefits for the minimum living wage.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Mandatory first pillar: 5.3% employee salary contributions - Uri Compensation Fund collects payments and calculates AVH annuities - Contribution gaps: recoverable through additional payments - Supplementary benefits cover the minimum living allowance if insufficient income
## Key facts - **What**: First pillar (AVS) managed by cantonal clearing house - When: Contributions paid throughout the working life; reference age pension - Where: Canton Uri; UFAS offices for federal matters - Who: Employees, employers, freelancers (each contributes their own %) - Rate: 5.3% of salary for employees; 5.3% employers; 10.6% self-employed - Protection: Complementary services for those who do not reach a vital minimum - Institution: BSV (Federal Office of Social Insurance) coordinates at federal level
### The first pillar in Canton Uri
In Canton Uri, as in all Swiss cantons, the first pillar of social security (AVS) represents the basis of the protection system for old age and disability. The cantonal compensation fund, a federal body at regional level, is responsible for the collection of compulsory contributions and the calculation of annuities.
AVS contributions follow a precise pattern: employees pay 5.3% of their salary, employers an identical percentage (5.3%), while the self-employed pay 10.6% of their income. This structure ensures that funding ## Complementary services: the role in the protection of the vital minimum
In Canton Uri, the supplementary benefit system (CCP) acts as a safety net for policyholders whose AVS annuity is not sufficient to cover basic living expenses: housing, food, healthcare, utilities. CCPs are paid in conjunction with the AVS annuity, to supplement it up to the level of the vital minimum. The amount varies depending on the personal situation (single person, couple, households with children) and the actual regional costs in the canton.
It is not a fixed amount universal benefit: each case is evaluated on the basis of concrete need. Those who receive an AVS annuity close to the limit but still insufficient can apply for CCPs to bridge the gap. The recognition is automatic if the application is submitted correctly and the documents are complete.
### Combination AVS + LPP + complementary performance
The first pillar (AVS) is flanked by the [secondo pilastro (LPP, Cassa pensioni)](nav:pension), which collects contributions from employees and employers in proportion to the coordinated salary. LPP contributions vary by age group: - 25–34 years: 7% - 35–44 years: 10% - 45–54 years: 15% - 55 years and over: 18% (up to the reference age)
When the first and second pillars together do not reach the ** vital minimum **, the CCPs intervene. Those who have integrated with a third pillar (3a) further strengthen their protection, even if it is not mandatory.
### Practical procedure in the Canton

The first step is to verify your contribution record with the compensation fund of Canton Uri. You can obtain an extract (contribution account) by presenting yourself directly at the counters or by requesting the documentation by mail. The extract shows year by year the registered payments, any gaps, and the number of accumulated contribution years.
If there are gaps in the extract, the fund informs about the deadlines for recovery. The retroactive payment of missing contributions must be accompanied by an invoice from the fund itself with an amount indexed according to federal directives. The terms for recovery are limited: it is not possible to recover gaps of more than five years without proven reasons of force majeure.
### Application for supplementary benefits: step-by-step
**1. Verify eligibility**: The AVS pension (plus any other pension from LPP, third pillar, or private policies) must not cover the minimum cost of living in Canton Uri. If the sum is lower, you have the right to submit an application.
2. Gather documents: Extract your UFAS account from the federal portal (e-service authentication), obtain your AVS pension certificate from the Uri cantonal fund, and prepare a detailed statement of monthly expenses (rent with contract, health insurance premiums, utilities, food).
3. Complete the application: Download the application form from the Canton Uri administration website. There are no unified federal forms; each canton has its own administrative procedure.
4. Submit: Send the application by mail or deliver it to the competent counter. Check the deadline: usually the application must arrive before December 31st for recognition of the previous year.
5. Settlement: Within 30–60 days from the complete application, if everything is in order, the benefit is recognized and monthly payment begins.
### Online tools for calculation and monitoring
The [salary and tax calculator](nav:calculator) allows you to simulate social deductions (including AVS/AI/IPG), but for an accurate estimate of your future pension, it is advisable to contact the compensation fund of Canton Uri directly. UFAS also offers on the federal portal (www.ufas.admin.ch) an online contribution data extraction service through e-service authentication with a Swiss digital certificate. This is the quickest way to obtain your contribution account without having to travel.
For questions about the contribution recovery procedure, specific gaps, or your future pension situation, the compensation fund remains the main point of contact: it understands local dynamics and can advise on the best completion strategy. ### The Federal Framework
In the canton of Uri, as in the whole of Switzerland, the rules on rentals are governed by federal law. Article 253 of the Code of Obligations sets standards that protect both tenants and owners. This means that the basic rules are identical from Uri to Geneva, from Basel to Lugano. There are no cantonal exceptions on filing, contesting or cancellation: federal law prevails.
For renters in Uri, this uniformity is an advantage. If you know the federal rules, you know them everywhere in Switzerland. But it also requires precision: a poorly drafted cancellation or a deposit above the federal limit can create disputes.
### Security deposit: the constraint in favour of the tenant
The security deposit may not exceed three months of monthly rent. If ## Termination: the cantonal form is mandatory
Anyone wishing to terminate a lease (tenant or landlord) must comply with the minimum notice period established by federal law and communicate their intent via registered letter (handed over personally or by official mail). This is where Canton Uri's rules apply: the termination is ONLY valid if delivered using an official cantonal form—not on a blank sheet of paper or via email.
Failure to use the official form renders the termination legally invalid. This protects the receiving party from the unintentional loss of an important communication. In Uri, the form is available from the cantonal authority responsible for rental matters or online via the cantonal administration's website.
Termination periods (from federal law): - 1 month during the first year of the lease - 2 months from the second to the ninth year - 3 months from the tenth year onward

Imagine this scenario: a tenant signs a lease in Uri. The landlord communicates a monthly rent. The tenant believes the price is excessive compared to similar properties in the area. They file a formal contestation with the conciliation authority within 30 days.
The authority receives the appeal, summons both parties (tenant and landlord), and attempts mediation. It gathers information on market rents in the area (via databases or expert appraisals). If the parties fail to agree, the authority issues a record of attempted conciliation, and the case proceeds to the cantonal court for a final ruling.
During this process, the tenant typically continues paying the contested rent (as a deposit, to be refunded or offset at the dispute's conclusion). If the authority reduces the rent, any overpayment may generate credits on your 'tax return'.

Canton Uri has its own rental conciliation authority. This body resolves disputes over rents, deposits, and terminations before cases go to court. Appeal timelines and procedures follow the federal principle, identical across Switzerland.
